chunks: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafith narrated to us. He said: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Khalaf narrated to us. He said: Sahl ibn Amer narrated to us. He said: Zafir ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Sharik from Abi Ishaq. He said: I said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him):
What is the meaning of the saying of the Prophet (may God bless him and his family): 'Whoever takes me as a master, then Ali is his master'? He said: He informed them that he is the Imam after him.

key_terms.الإمام: Imam — the divinely appointed leader and guide of the Muslim community after the Prophet
key_terms.غدير خم: Ghadir Khumm — the location where the Prophet made his famous declaration about Ali's authority
key_terms.مولى: Mawla — master, guardian, patron; the key term in the Hadith of Ghadir, indicating authority and leadership

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about the meaning of the Hadith of Ghadir?
ai.summary: In this hadith, narrated on the day of Ghadir Khumm in the shrine of Imam al-Rida, Abu Ishaq asks Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), the 4th Imam, to explain the meaning of the famous hadith of Ghadir: 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa-hadha Aliyyun mawlahu.' The Imam's succinct interpretation is that the Prophet was explicitly designating Ali as the Imam (leader) after him, establishing the doctrine of Imamate succession. This interpretation is central to Shia theology and was narrated in the context of the Ghadir Khumm commemoration.
